title: Shooter (capstone)
summary: Everything composed at scale: a parameterized Enemy system whose instances are born and destroyed mid-game, a Boss whose three phases are HSM parents with idle/fire leaves, and an orchestrator running waves, the boss fight, and a push$/pop$ pause.
teaches: Dynamic multi-instance lifecycle ($Spawning→$Active→$Dying→$Gone) · three-phase Boss HSM with HP-threshold transitions · 42 state-local variables under load
controls: Arrows/WASD move · hold SPACE fire · P pause · SPACE start · R restart

machines.title: Shooter — the orchestrator
machines.blurb: Attract → Playing (wave scheduling, enemy spawn signals) → BossFight → Victory / GameOver, with pause as a push$/pop$ interrupt from either combat state. Owns the player, the boss, and the driver-populated enemies list — the same composition pattern as Pac-Man's scheduler, at twice the scale.

machines.title: Boss — a three-phase HSM
machines.blurb: $PhaseOne / $PhaseTwo / $PhaseThree are HSM parents, each with idle/fire attack-pattern leaves; HP thresholds drive the phase transitions, and each phase's state-local timers reset on entry. The deepest hierarchy in the collection: game → phase → attack leaf.

machines.title: Enemy — instances with a lifecycle
machines.blurb: @@Enemy(kind, hp, fire_rate, points) — spawned in waves, each instance runs $Spawning → $Active → $Dying → $Gone and is then discarded. Where Pac-Man's four ghosts live forever, Shooter churns compartment sets — the create/destroy path of the runtime, per language. The panel tracks the first live enemy.

machines.title: Player — hit/invulnerability window
machines.blurb: Alive → Exploding → Invulnerable → back to Alive (or Dead) — the classic damage loop, with the invulnerability grace window as a timed state.
